newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy state of emergency not as serious as sounds.
newsitem.headline: Italy state of emergency not as serious as sounds.

text.p: Italy said a "state of emergency" declared on Wednesday to cope with a flood of refugees from Albania was nothing more than a way to make funds available fast to cope with a humanitarian crisis.
The statement by the Interior Ministry was apparently intended to remove any misunderstanding abroad that the measure might mean troops on the streets and tough security measures.
It noted that similar declarations had been made in the past, usually in response to floods, landslides and other natural disasters.
In the case of the Albanian refugee crisis, the emergency allows the government to make 61 billion lire ($36 million) in public funds available swiftly to cover relief operations.
It was announced as the number of Albanians who have fled their country's anarchy by crossing the Adriatic to Italy rose to more than 10,000 in less than a week.
Diplomatic sources said Italian embassies in several countries received a spate of anxious inquiries from tour operators and other telephone callers about what the "state of emergency" meant.
